subject: High rate of 429/5xx and timeout loop after q4_8s-v2 rollout
messages:
From: Caroline Meyers <caroline@retailco.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@retailco.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Production: surge of 429/5xx + timeouts after model update

Neha —

We started seeing a serious increase in 429s and 5xx responses starting ~07:15 PDT after the model update your team did (q4_8s-v2). Our client-facing ingestion queue is backing up and many requests are timing out at 30s. We've attached a sample of request_id traces and the edge NLB logs.

Immediate impact: ad serving latency doubled for certain catalogs; customers are reporting timeouts. This is causing churn on a small subset of traffic (10% of requests) but critical paths are affected.

Can you confirm rollback or mitigation steps? Our SREs recommended throttling client retries but we want Redwood to advise since the spike began right after your rollout.

Attaching: retailco-logs-0308.zip (500KB)

— Caroline
VP, Platform Operations
RetailCo
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Meyers <caroline@retailco.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: surge of 429/5xx + timeouts after model update

Caroline —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for sending the logs. I'm sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as SEV-1 and have engineering looking immediately.

Short plan:
- Marcus and Rishi are triaging kernel/quantization interactions and will review the q4_8s-v2 rollout config.
- If we see the serving layer returning amplified client retries or head-of-line blocking, we'll roll back the quantization profile within the hour.
- I'll share an incident bridge and a short summary for your execs in 30 minutes.

Neha
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: surge of 429/5xx + timeouts after model update

On Mon, Mar 8, 2027 at 08:12, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus and Rishi are triaging kernel/quantization interactions and will review the q4_8s-v2 rollout config.

Preliminary: we've confirmed elevated tail latencies and a correlated increase in GPU kernel queues for the model family retail-gpt-3b. The new q4_8s-v2 profile reduces memory but changed the fused-attn-opt kernel selection for short sequences. That kernel path shows serialization under certain batch shapes; it causes longer per-request service times for the hotkey prefix pattern RetailCo uses.

Symptoms we're seeing:
- 5xx errors originate from backend timeouts after N attempts to schedule on a busy kernel thread.
- Client retries collide (clients are doing exponential backoff but aggressive), creating a thundering set of requests to the same prefix keys. This amplifies throughput pressure.

Immediate mitigation we can attempt (in order):
1) Pin RetailCo to the previous quantization profile (q4_8s-v1) for the dedicated pool (safe rollback).
2) Apply a hotpath patch to prefer the older attention kernel for short sequences while we debug.
3) Temporarily rate-limit identical-prefix requests by token signature at the edge (coordinated with RetailCo SREs).

I'll try rolling RetailCo back to q4_8s-v1 in the next 20–30 minutes and will post the control-plane link to the incident.

— Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: serving-profile-q4_8s-v2.png
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: surge of 429/5xx + timeouts after model update

Neha / team —

Rolled back RetailCo's serving config to q4_8s-v1 on the dedicated pool at 08:46 PDT. Early metrics: 429 and 5xx rates dropping on the primary route from 4.8% -> 0.8% over the next 8 minutes. Latency tail is normalizing.

Notes: while rollback reduced errors, we still see elevated retry amplification from clients that retried aggressively earlier. Recommend RetailCo temporarily patch client retry jitter to reduce bursts (we can provide guidance). We'll also deploy a fix to the kernel selector tomorrow to avoid the fused-attn-opt path for their short-prefix workload.

I'll keep the incident open until we observe 30 minutes of stable SLOs.

— Rishi
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Meyers <caroline@retailco.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: surge of 429/5xx + timeouts after model update

Caroline —

Update: we rolled RetailCo back to the previous quantization profile (q4_8s-v1) at 08:46 PDT. After the rollback the 5xx/429 rate decreased and tail latency is back within your SLOs. Marcus and Rishi have a remediation plan:

- Short-term: we will hold RetailCo on q4_8s-v1 until the kernel selector fix is in (target: 2027-03-09 morning deploy).
- Mid-term: patch to kernel selector to avoid fused-attn-opt for short sequences / hotkey prefixes (testing in progress).
- We'll share a simple retry guidance doc for your SREs to reduce amplification during recovery windows.

Apologies again for the disruption. Please let me know if you want an executive readout; Laura can join for a 30-min sync.

Thanks for the patience — we're keeping the incident open and monitoring for another hour.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
